headline: Iron ore drops to a two-year low
detail: Singapore iron ore fell about 1% to $89.45 a ton early Tuesday, the lowest since September 2024, as Chinese mills hold back on restocking and more ore supply is due. Weaker ore usually drags on steel and ferrous scrap prices.

headline: Teck copper mine strike rolls into its first full week
detail: More than 1,200 Steelworkers remain off the job at Highland Valley, Canada's largest open-pit copper mine, over pay, pensions and staffing. A long strike would tighten North American copper supply and support copper scrap.

headline: Nucor: scrap costs flat, fourth quarter steady
detail: Nucor earned $5.80 a share in Q3 and paid an average $421 per gross ton for scrap and substitutes, about the same as Q2. It sees Q4 earnings flat to slightly higher, a sign the biggest US scrap buyer expects steady mill demand.

headline: Fed meeting starts today; hold expected, December hike likely
detail: The Fed announces Wednesday at 1pm CT with the rate at 3.75%–4.0% and about 90% odds of no change, but futures put a December hike near 73% after September CPI hit 3.7%. A hawkish tone would firm the dollar and weigh on metals.

headline: Copper edges up toward $6.55 on renewed AI buying
detail: COMEX copper closed Monday near $6.54 a pound and firmed early Tuesday as AI and data-center optimism returned. Whether the US taxes refined copper imports before the midterms is still undecided.

headline: China's copper stocks drain; import premium at 11-year high
detail: Shanghai exchange copper stocks fell more than 25% to about 54,000 tons and the Yangshan import premium hit $168 a ton, highest since 2014. Strong Chinese buying supports world copper prices even as LME stocks sit near 273,000 tons.

headline: Zinc jumps to a two-week high on tight stocks
detail: LME zinc rose about 2% to roughly $3,820 as inventories fall, Peru output drops and power costs stay high; cash zinc trades over $100 above three-month metal. Tight zinc supports galvanized and die-cast scrap values.

headline: US and Canada talk about easing steel and auto tariffs
detail: Commerce Secretary Lutnick and Canada's LeBlanc are working on a deal to trim Section 232 tariffs (up to 50% on steel, 25% on autos), possibly before the Nov. 3 midterms. A deal could let more Canadian steel in and cool US steel and scrap prices.

headline: China factory profits rise 14.4% in September
detail: Chinese industrial profits grew at the fastest pace since June, led by AI-related and mining sectors, while consumer industries lagged. Better profits help metals demand but lower the odds of new stimulus.

headline: Gold gets back above $4,000 as oil cools
detail: Spot gold closed near $4,016 Monday, up about 0.5%, as talk of Hormuz diplomacy pulled Brent down to about $116 and eased inflation worries. It slipped toward $3,998 early Tuesday ahead of the Fed.

headline: Silver slides 2% overnight; Fresnillo output falls
detail: Silver dropped to about $52.73 early Tuesday, more than 20% under its August high, with $50 seen as the next support. Top producer Fresnillo said Q3 output fell 11.6% from a year ago.

headline: Platinum and palladium fall more than 2% early Tuesday
detail: Platinum dropped about $40 to near $1,486 and palladium about $23 to $1,003 overnight as oil and yields eased and traders waited on the Fed; China's platinum futures fell 2%. Lower PGM prices cut what converters are worth.

headline: Converter buyers still average about $90 a unit
detail: RRCats' national average held near $90 a converter on Oct. 26, with large foreign cats at $90–$450 and regular domestic at $20–$128. Expect softer bids if platinum's overnight drop holds.

headline: Indonesia cuts its nickel benchmark price 2.9%
detail: Indonesia lowered its late-October nickel reference price by $475 to about $15,848 a ton as new mining quotas push ore prices down. LME nickel's official price slipped 1% to $15,535; cheaper nickel weighs on stainless scrap.

headline: Aluminum steady as LME stocks keep shrinking
detail: LME aluminum's official price edged up to $3,047.50 and exchange stocks fell another 1,750 tons to about 234,000. Prices are still far below June's peak on expected extra supply from China and Indonesia.

headline: US hot-rolled coil holds near $1,383
detail: Midwest HRC futures added $2 to about $1,383 a short ton Monday, close to four-year highs as tariffs keep imports out. Strong sheet prices keep mills hungry for prime scrap.

headline: World steel output dips 0.2% in September; US up 4.3%
detail: Global crude steel output was 142.4 million tons in September; China was flat at 73.6 million and the US rose 4.3% to 7.2 million. Higher US output means steady demand for scrap from EAF mills.

headline: Mills expected to pay more for ferrous scrap in November
detail: Market players surveyed by Steel Market Update expect November ferrous scrap prices to rise. Firm steel prices and steady mill runs back that up, though iron ore's slide is a risk.

headline: China's copper scrap imports jump 33% in September
detail: China imported about 237,000 tons of copper scrap in September, up 33% from August, as its import window opened; US shipments are recovering from a very low base. Strong Chinese demand helps support copper scrap prices.

headline: Alsip-area copper bids tick up a penny
detail: MetalRecap's Alsip-area averages show #1 copper at $4.76 and #2 at $4.60 a pound, with heavy steel at 9 cents. Local bids are moving in step with COMEX.

headline: Stellantis and Ford report earnings Wednesday
detail: Stellantis posts Q3 results early Wednesday after cutting dealer stock and planned summer shutdowns; Ford reports later that day. Production plans drive the flow of factory steel and aluminum scrap.

headline: Jeep Wrangler plant in Toledo stops after nearby chemical leak
detail: Stellantis sent Toledo Assembly workers home after a chemical release at a nearby tank facility. Dealers hold about 156 days of Wranglers, so a short pause won't hurt supply much, but lost shifts mean less factory scrap.

headline: Stellantis Canada workers authorize a strike
detail: Unifor members voted 97.3% for a strike mandate covering more than 9,000 Stellantis workers; Windsor Assembly would be hit first. A strike would cut Canadian vehicle output and steel demand.

headline: Builder confidence falls to lowest since 2012
detail: The NAHB index dropped 3 points to 29 in October, with 43% of builders cutting prices as mortgage rates sit near 7.4%. Weak homebuilding means less demand for copper wire, pipe and steel.

headline: Housing starts fall 5.2% in September
detail: Starts dropped to a 1.22 million annual pace and single-family permits fell 4%. New-home sales come out Tuesday morning for another read on construction demand.

headline: US-Mexico trade deal stalls over 50% steel tariffs
detail: Talks with Mexico have stalled on how much to cut US steel and aluminum tariffs, and may wait until after the midterms. High tariffs keep US steel prices, and scrap demand, elevated.

headline: Oil eases; Brent settles near $116
detail: Brent fell 0.8% to $115.81 and WTI 1.7% to about $101.57 Monday as Middle East diplomacy cooled fears. Lower oil eases inflation pressure and the case for Fed hikes, which helps metals.
